title: Iagon & Würth: Platform for Secure 3D Printing and Intellectual Property Management

ms.promise:
Objective: 
Establish a comprehensive design blueprint for the royalty tracking system. This includes detailing technical requirements, architecture, and a secure decentralized storage plan within the project and for managing transactions and distributing royalties for IP-protected 3D files.
Outputs:
・Technical overview: documentation of planned system architecture, including architecture diagrams, data flow, and security protocols, integration plan with the Iagon decentralized storage network, where applicable.
・Royalty and Transaction tracking: Design outline for tracking and settlement of digital licenses to print, associated transactions, and royalty percentages for IP owners in a smart contract.
・Initial Blockchain Solution Selection: A range of blockchain approaches within Cardano ecosystem will be assessed based on scalability, security, cost-efficiency, and alignment with project objectives.
・Data Management Plan: Decide on how IP-protected 3D files are stored with the Iagon solution, determine encryption standards and access control mechanisms. Share research discovery findings and reasoning on decision regarding DMP.
ms.criteria:
・The architectural design (diagrams and system workflows) must be reviewed and approved by Iagon and Würth teams.
・A plan for transaction management and royalty tracking, with justification for the chosen solution.
・An analysis of the Cardano L1, Partner Chain, Hydra, or a combination of these blockchains, with the final selection validated by the Iagon and Wurth teams. 
・The data management plan outlines the platform’s approach for encryption, decentralized file storage, and access workflows, and is signed off by Iagon and Würth.
ms.report:
This Proof of Achievement confirms the completion of Milestone 1. The milestone focused on preparing and validating the initial technical, architectural, blockchain, royalty tracking, and data management documentation for the enterprise pilot between Iagon and Würth.
The project is a closed-source, corporate-grade enterprise pilot. Therefore, sensitive implementation details, security-specific information, infrastructure details, and partner-confidential information have been generalized or redacted where needed. The submitted documentation verifies milestone completion while respecting enterprise confidentiality requirements.

・The Milestone 1 documentation is published in the public GitHub repository - https://github.com/IagonAS/iagon-wurth-catalyst-public/tree/main/docs/milestone-1

The Introduction document includes the milestone overview, evidence package structure, confidentiality note, and reviewer-facing context for the submitted materials.
A. Output: Technical Overview

Acceptance criteria:
・The architectural design, including diagrams and system workflows, has been reviewed by the Iagon and Würth teams as part of the Milestone 1 documentation package.

Evidence:
・Technical Overview document - https://github.com/IagonAS/iagon-wurth-catalyst-public/blob/main/docs/milestone-1/01-technical-ov

ms.report:
This Proof of Achievement submission covers Milestone 2 of the Iagon & Würth: Smart Contract Design and Initial Service Development.
The evidence is organized around the agreed Milestone 2 outputs: the smart contract prototype, royalty mechanism, off-chain API prototype, API endpoint specification, and walkthrough video.
The Milestone 2 documentation is available in the public GitHub repository, with supporting demonstration material and partner review confirmation provided separately.
A. Output: Smart Contract Prototype Report
・A functional smart contract prototype was delivered for Milestone 2. The prototype translates the licensing and royalty design validated in Milestone 1 into a working set of Cardano smart contracts.
・The prototype consists of four interrelated Cardano smart contracts written in Aiken / Plutus V3:
・Genesis contract
・Reference contract
・Vault contract
・Bucket contract
・Together, these contracts demonstrate the required Milestone 2 smart contract behaviours:
・token issuance;
・access control logic;
・royalty distribution.
・The prototype includes system identity issuance, vault and bucket identifier issuance, and royalty credit issuance through IOU tokens. It also separates keeper-controlled administrative actions from operator-controlled day-to-day royalty operations.

Acceptance criteria
・The smart contract prototype has been completed and documented as a functional mock contract that simulates token issuance, access control, and royalty logic.
・The report explains how the prototype addresses the required Milestone 2 themes:
・token issuance through the Genesis, Vault, Bucket, and IOU token flows;
・access control through keeper multisig, per-container custody, and scoped operator authority;
・royalty distribution through batched IOU issuance and atomic payout logic.
・The prototype was also exercised through a happy-path execution on Cardano preprod, covering:

・Genesis
・Vault Creation
・Vault Fill
・Bucket Creation
・IOU Mint
・Bucket Payout

Evidence

ms.promise:
Objective: 
Develop APIs and UX to integrate the tokenization platform with Würth’s DIS (Digital Inventory Services), enabling seamless user interactions with 3D IP files. Additionally, design the Iagon storage connector for integration with the DIS. This milestone establishes the user-facing integration and sets the foundation for end-user interactions.

Outputs:
・API Documentation: Initial API specifications detailing endpoint structures, input/output parameters, and integration logic for DIS.
・Integration Test Results: Detailed test reports validating data exchange, performance, and system response between the platform and DIS.
・UX Designs: Wireframes or clickable prototypes showing end-to-end user flows for ordering and 3D printing interactions. These designs will be finalized and delivered regardless of implementation needs. If UI already present, screenshots may be provided instead.
・Storage Connector Design: Technical documentation describing the architecture and design plan for the Iagon storage connector with Würth’s DIS.
ms.criteria:
・API documentation is complete and reviewed by internal technical teams at Iagon and Würth with signed doc as confirmation.
・Integration testing with DIS produces logs and test results demonstrating data exchange, performance characteristics, and system response, including procedures for replication. Reviewer access to documentation will be granted.
・UX design flows are developed in accordance with the original proposal and validated through feedback and usability testing. A UX report will be provided, outlining decisions and designs, regardless of platform deployment status.
・Design documents
ms.report:
This Proof of Achievement submission covers Milestone 3 of the Iagon & Würth: Platform for Secure 3D Printing and Intellectual Property Management project, titled “DIS/Storefront Integration API and UI Development.”
The evidence is organized around the agreed Milestone 3 outputs: integration API documentation, integration test results, UX documentation, the Iagon storage connector design, and a video walkthrough.
The Milestone 3 documentation and supporting evidence are available in the public GitHub repository. Partner review confirmation and any credentials required to access protected API documentation are provided separately to assigned reviewers through the Catalyst team and are not included in this public submission.
・Complete Milestone 3 evidence package - https://github.com/IagonAS/iagon-wurth-catalyst-public/tree/main/docs/milestone-3

A. Output: Integration API Documentation
The Integration API Documentation describes the interface between Würth’s ORSY Connect storefront and the Iagon royalty orchestration platform. It covers the endpoints used to register vendors, create 3D-print licences, and submit orders. For each part of the interface, the document records the request and response fields, field mappings, authentication conventions, sample payloads, error responses, and the resulting platform actions.
The document also records how the integration scope was resolved during implementation. ORSY Connect is the storefront and sends vendor, licence, and order data to the orchestrator. DIS is a storage consumer and does not call the orchestrator. Its connection to Iagon is handled through the storage connector described in Output D.
The documentation includes the design-stage interface of the storage connector and explains how the connector maps the enterprise object-storage model used by the consumer to Iagon storage operations.
